messages:
oliver: Heads-up: ran into a weird context propagation bug when the AsyncClient spins up a background keepalive task during import.

oliver: Behavior: we set a request_id contextvar in FastAPI dependency, but in logs the background refresh task loses that context and ends up calling auth refresh with an empty request_id. Auth server logs show missing headers.

oliver: Stack trace snippet: 

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/_client.py", line 410, in _refresh_loop
    await self._refresh_token()
  File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/_client.py", line 332, in _refresh_token
    headers = {"x-request-id": request_id.get()}
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/contextvars.py", line 328, in get
RuntimeError: ContextVar has no value

priyanka: Oof. That matches: if AsyncClient.__init__ creates a background task at import and that task is created outside the request context, contextvars won't be set. How is the keepalive started?

oliver: We do `self._keepalive_task = asyncio.create_task(self._refresh_loop())` in __init__ if keepalive=True. So background task may be bound to whatever context exists at import (often none).

rafi: Two separate problems colliding: 1) import-time event loop capture (uvicorn reload / pytest-xdist), 2) contextvar propagation into background tasks. The fix for (2) is to wrap background task creation with contextvars.copy_context().run(lambda: asyncio.create_task(...)) so the current context is captured. But at import there's no relevant context anyway.

taylor: For our usage pattern we actually want the refresh task to run without request-scoped context; it shouldn't read request_id. But using contextvar.get without default leads to RuntimeError. Maybe the refresh code should use `.get(None)` or catch LookupError and fallback.

mel: Agreed. Two possible SDK fixes: 
- Never create background tasks in __init__; require explicit `await client.start()` or lazy init.
- If background tasks are created in an async context, ensure they capture contextvars explicitly (copy_context).
- Defensive code: never call contextvar.get() without default in background tasks that are not request-scoped.

priyanka: For typing and DX, also add an explicit lifecycle API: `await client.start()` and `await client.stop()` plus `AsyncClient.lazy()` constructor so sampleapps don't shoot themselves in the foot. That also makes shutdown ordering clearer.

rafi: For interim fix: change refresh loop to `rid = request_id.get(None)` and skip using it if None. Log a debug line. Add a test that sets a contextvar in request and asserts background task doesn't crash.

taylor: There's also an awkward interaction with contextvars and set_task_factory in pytest plugins. We should add tests running under pytest-xdist and with uvicorn --reload to prevent regressions.

oliver: I opened a draft PR with a minimal repro and tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/462 (WIP). The PR adds lazy constructor + fixes to refresh loop and copies context when start() is run inside a request.

mel: Nice. Also please ensure `__aenter__`'s return type is "AsyncClient" in annotations so `async with client as c:` works with type checkers. And add docs for recommended patterns in sampleapps.

priyanka: One more: document the reason in migration notes: why creating AsyncClient at import can leak event loop and context problems, and show examples: `client = AsyncClient(lazy=True)` or `client = None` + create in `startup`.

infra-bot: CI: test/async/contextvar-repro passed on branch fix/contextvar-lazy-462.

oliver: Thanks all. After PR merges I'll update onboarding sample app to `AsyncClient(lazy=True)` and add a short troubleshooting FAQ entry. :raised_hands:
